ORIGIN.quote: **Attribution is hard but not impossible.** Identity churn (thousands of labels, rotating Azure egress IPs) mimics anonymity, but content signatures (fixed sequences, shared page vocabulary, `OpenAI*` naming) make runs clusterable.
ORIGIN.reason: A reader comes away with abundant OpenAI-bearing evidence — `OpenAIResearchSec2028`, `ChatGPTAug11`, `OpenAIResearcher`, `AgentAug25OAI`, Azure/Microsoft egress ranges — but the report never once says or implies that any of it indicates OpenAI as the swarm's operator; the naming is used only as evidence of automation, of many parallel runs, and of run-to-run clusterability, and the Limitations section flatly states "I cannot identify the specific evaluation or lab running these agents" without naming a candidate. It sits just above the 0.2 anchor because the attribution paragraph does place `OpenAI*` naming in an explicitly attribution-framed context, but it falls short of 0.4 because OpenAI is never floated as a possible source and then dismissed — it is simply never proposed at all.
